extraction_notes: Direct filesystem reads + git history (`git log -S`, `git log -p`) + ripgrep for symbol/string occurrences. GitNexus MCP was preferred per ADR-0007 v2.x, but for an indexed feature-pipeline repo dominated by Markdown agent contracts, shell scripts, Python audit modules, and JSON config (no large compiled-language symbol surface), direct Read/Grep is the higher-fidelity path. Where blast-radius queries would have used Cypher in a service-style repo, here the dependents are reviewer-callers in the parent orchestrator skill (one file) — grep against that single file gives ground truth.

components.name: shared-document-reviewer
components.notes: Single largest reviewer in the project (26.7KB). Emits a structured verdict object at line 196 of its body, plus severity-tagged findings. Verdict-finding shape varies by doc_type — see report for the per-doc_type variants. Gate-0 mechanical validator dispatched via auditing-shared scripts; Gate-1 quality checks layered above it. The PRD's named subject for FR-1.

components.name: review-architecture-auditor
entry_points: Stage 8 Architecture Audit (after shared-document-reviewer passes the Blueprint at Gate 4)
components.notes: Emits a verdict from {fail, conditional_pass, pass} at line 129. Severity-to-verdict mapping is explicit at lines 135-137: BLOCKER→fail, MAJOR→conditional_pass, MINOR/INFO→pass. Output: architecture-audit-issues.json. The PRD's named subject for FR-1.

components.name: review-cross-artifact-auditor
entry_points: Stage 11 Cross-Artifact Audit (after Test Authoring; auditor-driven, no human gate)
components.notes: Emits a verdict from {fail, conditional_pass, pass, hard_capped} at line 148. Also emits a separate 'convergence' verdict ({converging, stalling, diverging, first_round}) at line 136 — this is structurally a second verdict in the same output payload. Severity rules deterministic; hard-cap triggers at round_number≥4 regardless of issue count. The PRD's named subject for FR-1.

components.name: execute-phase-quality-reviewer
entry_points: T7 transition (per_task_approved → phase_quality_active; once per phase after all tasks APPROVED)
components.notes: Emits a 5-dimensional verdict per Contract 2 of execution-pipeline-design-r1 Blueprint v5. Verdict enum: {PASS, NEEDS_RECONCILIATION, BLOCKER}. Findings array adjacent at line 44. PRD's named subject for FR-1. Per ADR-0033 surfaces Scope-Deviations as a fifth dimension.

components.name: finalize-deliverable-packager
components.notes: REVIEWER-SHAPED beyond the four PRD-named agents. Emits a verdict enum {PASS, BLOCK, REVIEW} at line 81 of its body. Adjacent fields: artifacts_present, artifacts_missing_required, artifacts_missing_conditional_unjustified, artifacts_unexpected, adr_cross_location_findings, reviewer_findings. The reviewer_findings field aggregates the shared-document-reviewer's findings on the archive (a chain rather than a fresh emission), but the verdict is the packager's own — making this a candidate for FR-1 scope completeness (see scope_completeness_finding).

components.name: execute-task-quality-handler
entry_points: T2 transition (per_task_active → quality_active; once per task after code-producer COMPLETED)
components.notes: REVIEWER-SHAPED beyond the four PRD-named agents. Emits a per-task verdict object (Contract 1 of execution-pipeline-design-r1 Blueprint v5). Status enum: {APPROVED, NEEDS_REVISION, STUB_DETECTED, BLOCKER}. Findings array at line 34 with severity {blocker, major, minor, info} and domain enumeration. Verdict_rationale field at line 46. The verdict-shape is the cleanest verdict+findings pair in the agent inventory — should be in FR-1 scope per the intent doc's framing.

components.name: synth-critic
entry_points: Synthesis batch processing (one batch per invocation, parallel)
components.notes: Per-claim verdict enum: {verified, unverifiable, contradicted, single_sourced} at line 32-36. This is a verdict-per-claim shape (one batch → many verdicts inside a critique JSON), not a single overall verdict per invocation. The intent doc's framing 'verdict+findings pair' is plausibly interpretable to include or exclude this shape — surfaced for design-claude-code's scope decision.

components.name: finalize-reconciler
entry_points: Reconciliation stage; up to 4 cycles per ADR-0017
components.notes: Consumes verdicts; emits a 'convergence verdict' (line 142, choosing from {converging, stalling, diverging, terminal}) plus a dispatch JSON. NOT a fresh verdict+findings pair in the FR-1 sense — its job is downstream dispatch authoring, not artifact verdict-issuance. Mentioned here so design-claude-code can confirm exclusion.

components.name: recipe-feature-pipeline (parent orchestrator)
entry_points: Whole-pipeline orchestration; called by Claude Code session as the operator-invoked skill
components.notes: The actual parent orchestrator per ADR-0044's flatten decision. 629 lines. Dispatches reviewers at 5 explicit invocation points (count of 'shared-document-reviewer' occurrences in body: 19; reviewer-arch: 4; reviewer-cross-artifact: 4; phase-quality-reviewer: 5). The scope_class is read from intent-clarification.md frontmatter at line 350 inside the Deliverable Packaging step (Stage 12), but FR-2's self-check needs it at the earliest dispatch point — that's a structural finding for design-claude-code.

components.name: execute-orchestrator (advisor)
components.framework: Claude Code sub-agent (advisor only per ADR-0044)
components.notes: ADR-0044 flattened execution-phase dispatch into the parent. This file is now an advisor / canonical state-machine reference. The 12-substantive-state machine table lives here (T0..T13). FR-2's self-check candidate site is NOT here — it must live in the parent recipe-feature-pipeline.

components.name: auditing-mcp skill
components.framework: Claude Code skill family-coordinator (graduated per ADR-0042)
entry_points: Sub-skill family slot reserved but empty
components.notes: Hosts 14 Python scripts: audit_mcp.py (coordinator), 10 OP-rule scripts (audit_op1..audit_op10), plus check_toxic_combinations.py, scan_mcp_secrets.py, validate_mcp_config.py. Each OP rule has a uniform contract: takes path-to-.mcp.json positional, prints JSON findings object to stdout, returns exit 1 if findings else 0 (exit 2 on internal error). Severity tokens: BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR, NIT. FR-3's new rule lands as audit_op11_*.py following this pattern. References/ has 4 docs: mcp-spec.md, toxic-combinations.md, anti-patterns.md, common-failures.md.

components.name: .mcp.json
entry_points: Claude Code parses this at session start; six mcpServers entries
dependencies: env vars: CONTEXT7_API_KEY, EXA_API_KEY, GITNEXUS_TAG, TFE_TOKEN
components.notes: Six servers registered (not seven): actionlint-mcp, context7, exa, gitnexus, serena, terraform-mcp. mcp-openapi-schema absent (removed 2026-05-25 in commit bed4941 per the Gate-3 user-direction confirmation; see deprecation_finding). Each entry uses env-block indirection only (passes OP-1 + OP-9 + OP-10 cleanly). Both context7 and exa use type:http; the four others use stdio with command+args.

components.name: .devcontainer/postCreate.sh
components.notes: set -euo pipefail. Idempotency via .install-sentinel-<server>-<version> files in .claude/runtime/. Currently installs four OSS-local MCP servers (serena, actionlint-mcp, terraform-mcp, gitnexus) and runs auth probes against the two HTTP servers (context7, exa). The script's head comment is explicit that mcp-openapi-schema was removed 2026-05-24 per postmortem. The GitNexus install function (install_gitnexus) is the FR-4 dry-run's natural insertion site — sits between the sentinel check and the npm install -g step, lines ~127-150. components.name: .devcontainer/versions.env
entry_points: sourced by postCreate.sh and postStart.sh; ALSO duplicated in devcontainer.json containerEnv per the 2026-05-24 fix
components.notes: Five pins active: SERENA_VERSION=1.2.0, ACTIONLINT_MCP_SHA=7441fe04..., TERRAFORM_MCP_VERSION=0.5.2, GITNEXUS_TAG=1.6.5, plus an explicit mcp-openapi-schema removal rationale block (lines 18-24). components.name: .devcontainer/lib/log-mcp-event.sh
components.notes: Implements ADR-0037 event schema + ADR-0039 redaction-at-source. Default-fail-closed: if redaction logic fails, emits nothing rather than partially-redacted output. FR-4 + FR-3 + FR-5 diagnostics should use this helper for cross-mechanism consistency.

components.name: .github/workflows/ (greenfield)
components.notes: Confirmed absent: `ls .github/workflows/` returns 'No such file or directory'. FR-5 is the first workflow this project introduces. No precedent for SHA-pin, permissions:, concurrency, path-filter, claude-cli-install, or runner choice — design-cicd authors from KB defaults.

components.name: Issues/devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1-deferrals/register.md
components.notes: 282 lines. Rows B-1 (CI claude mcp list smoke) and H-4 (GitNexus dry-run) are ALREADY marked '(ADOPTED 2026-05-25 by pipeline-quickwins-hardening-r1 — see Issues/cross-artifact-divergence-detection-gap/proposal.md)' inline in their item-name cells (lines 56 and 141). The table has SEVEN ROWS today: Serena, mcp-openapi-schema, actionlint-mcp, terraform-mcp, gitnexus, Context7, Exa. cc.file_naming: Sub-agents at .claude/agents/<role>.md; skills at .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; KBs at .claude/skills/KB-<topic>/SKILL.md; auditing modules under .claude/skills/auditing-<scope>/.
cc.module_layout: Each agent is a single markdown file with YAML frontmatter (name, description, model, effort, tools, skills, memory) + body. Skills are directories with SKILL.md + optional references/ + scripts/ + examples/.
cc.agent_frontmatter: Fields: name, description (Claude-Code routing decisions), model (opus|sonnet|haiku), effort (low|medium|high), tools (allowlist; explicit list like [Read, Glob, Grep, ...] or whole-server mcp__<server>__*), skills (preloaded skill identifiers), memory (project|user|none).
cc.verdict_emission: Verdicts emit as a single string field inside a structured JSON output object — never free prose. Field name is consistently 'verdict' or 'status' depending on the agent. Verdict enums vary by agent: shared-document-reviewer (pass|conditional_pass|fail per doc_type), review-architecture-auditor (pass|conditional_pass|fail), review-cross-artifact-auditor (pass|conditional_pass|fail|hard_capped + a secondary convergence verdict), execute-phase-quality-reviewer (PASS|NEEDS_RECONCILIATION|BLOCKER), execute-task-quality-handler (APPROVED|NEEDS_REVISION|STUB_DETECTED|BLOCKER), finalize-deliverable-packager (PASS|BLOCK|REVIEW). Findings are always a JSON array adjacent to the verdict; finding objects have severity, file_path, message, and rule/domain identifiers — but the exact field names vary by reviewer.
cc.severity_taxonomy: BLOCKER (won't load / contractual violation) → MAJOR (works but degraded) → MINOR (deviates from best practice) → NIT/INFO (taste). Maps to verdicts deterministically: any BLOCKER → fail; any MAJOR (no BLOCKER) → conditional_pass; only MINOR/INFO → pass. See review-architecture-auditor.md lines 135-137 for the canonical mapping in the auditor family.
cc.logging: Sub-agents log via TaskUpdate at start and end of work (one line each, with mechanism-name + slug + outcome). The recipe-feature-pipeline orchestrator writes checkpoint.json and state-transitions.log.
cc.testing: No traditional unit-test framework. The auditing-* skills are exercised by running them against project artifacts (live audit); each audit_op*.py is independently invocable. Phase validators (auditing-shared/scripts/run_phase_checks.py) exercise the pipeline-output artifacts via a coordinator pattern.
cc.report_only_vs_enforcing: Auditing skills are report-only (write findings, do not modify configs); the orchestrator uses the findings to halt or dispatch. Reviewers are also report-only — they emit verdicts; the orchestrator acts on them. The 'enforce vs instruct' choice for FR-1/FR-2 must add an enforcing layer ON TOP of these report-only contracts (not modify the reviewer-output discipline itself).
cc.adr_authoring: Per FR-5 of execution-pipeline-design-r1 and ADR-0036, only design-composer authors ADRs. All other sub-agents may CITE ADRs but not AUTHOR them. The orchestrator hard-rejects ADR writes from any other path.

auditing-mcp.rule_naming: OP-N (where N is integer). OP-1 = env-block credential coverage; OP-2 = consumer-mapping; OP-3 = zero-mcp invariant; OP-4 = primary/fallback prose; OP-5 = lifecycle completeness; OP-6 = runtime log redaction; OP-7 = events schema; OP-8 = GitNexus-specific; OP-9 = URL-credential rejection; OP-10 = argv-leakage rejection. FR-3 lands as OP-11 by convention.
auditing-mcp.script_contract: Each OP script: takes one positional argument (path to .mcp.json), prints a JSON findings object to stdout {rule, name, target, findings:[], servers_checked}, returns exit 0 if no findings, exit 1 if any BLOCKER finding, exit 2 on internal error / bad input.
auditing-mcp.finding_format: {rule: 'OP-N', severity: BLOCKER|MAJOR|MINOR|NIT, server: <name>, field: <dotted-path>, message: <human-readable>}. FR-3 must include {prescribed_form, live_form, diff_dimension: argv|env|sentinel|...} in the finding to satisfy AC-FR-3-b.
auditing-mcp.rationale_placement: Each OP rule's rationale + anti-pattern catalog lives in .claude/skills/auditing-mcp/references/<topic>.md (mcp-spec.md, anti-patterns.md, common-failures.md, toxic-combinations.md). The skill's SKILL.md routing table maps dimension → reference file.

codespaces.shell_posture: set -euo pipefail at the top of every script (.devcontainer/postCreate.sh line 31; .devcontainer/postStart.sh; .devcontainer/lib/log-mcp-event.sh line 15).
codespaces.sentinel_naming: <server>@<version>.installed under .claude/runtime/install-sentinels/ — but the live postCreate.sh uses a different convention (.install-sentinel-<server>-<version>) under .claude/runtime/ directly. The ADR-0041 canonical form is the first; the live script's form is older. Surfaced as a minor discrepancy; FR-4 should NOT introduce a third convention.
codespaces.idempotency: sentinel-presence AND binary-on-PATH (the two-check pattern from ADR-0041 Decision item 3; live in postCreate.sh's check_installed() function lines 60-65). FR-4's dry-run should sit BEFORE the install step's sentinel short-circuit so it runs every rebuild.
codespaces.event_emission: log_mcp_event helper emits one JSONL record per install/probe to .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl. Event types per ADR-0037: install_complete, readiness_probe, structured_failure. Record fields: event, timestamp (ISO 8601), server, install_method, version, duration_ms, status, note (optional). FR-4 should emit an install_complete with status:ok|failed, NOT a new event type (NFR-13 compatibility).
codespaces.diagnostic_format: echo '[postCreate] <message>' >&2 for plain-text operator diagnostics; structured JSON via log_mcp_event for machine-readable events. The two streams are deliberately separate. FR-6 actionable diagnostics for FR-4 should follow this dual pattern: a single-line plain-text echo for operator legibility, plus a structured JSONL record for downstream consumers.

cicd.status: GREENFIELD — .github/workflows/ does not exist. No precedent for any workflow convention in this project.
cicd.kb_governance: KB-github-actions-platform/references/security.md and KB-github-actions-design/references/principles.md are the only inputs design-cicd has. The 'five non-negotiables' (SHA-pin third-party actions, least-privilege permissions, no untrusted input interpolation in run:, OIDC over long-lived keys, concurrency on deploy workflows) are the baseline for FR-5's first workflow.

documents.deferral_register_row_update: The convention observed in this register (rows B-1 and H-4) is to APPEND a parenthetical inside the Item-cell of the table row: '*(ADOPTED YYYY-MM-DD by <slug> — see <link>)*'. The Source, Why-excluded/deferred, and Re-examination-trigger cells are also updated: Why-excluded gets 'Now adopted: <summary>'; Re-examination-trigger gets 'Adopted by <slug>.'; Forgetting-risk gets 'Resolved by adoption.' The italics surround the inline marker. The register's TL;DR and counts are NOT incrementally updated row-by-row; the rationale is that the register is a snapshot doc, not a live ledger.
documents.frontmatter: All canonical docs carry YAML frontmatter with id, version, status, doc_type, generated, generated_by. Per KB-documentation-criteria.

known_issues.description: The execute-orchestrator agent is documented as 'advisor; non-invocable per ADR-0044' but still carries a full skills+tools+model frontmatter block that looks like an invocable agent. The frontmatter's `skills: [recipe-feature-pipeline, ...]` is explicitly a 'documentation-consistency anchor, NOT an invocation hint' per its own body. This dual existence is intentional but is the kind of thing FR-2's self-check could plausibly stumble over if it enumerates 'agents' rather than 'invocable agents'.

Sentinel naming inconsistency between ADR-0041 canonical form (<server>@<version>.installed under .claude/runtime/install-sentinels/) and the live postCreate.sh form (.install-sentinel-<server>-<version> directly under .claude/runtime/). The discrepancy is acknowledged in the ADR (I-DR-CS-001 resolution language) but the script's form is what shipped. FR-4 should NOT introduce a third convention; design-codespaces may choose to (a) align FR-4 with the script's current form, (b) trigger a cleanup of the script's form to match the ADR (out-of-scope per the carve-out), or (c) tolerate the discrepancy by not creating any sentinel in the dry-run.

The register documents an internal inconsistency: postCreate.sh's head-comment says 'Servers installed here (4 — post-2026-05-24 postmortem; was 5)' — 4 servers, not 5. The earlier description that mcp-openapi-schema removal would yield 5 OSS-local servers is now stale. ADR-0041's '5 OSS-local MCP servers' framing (Decision §1.b prereqs) needs the same update but is out-of-scope here.

scope_completeness_finding.purpose: FR-1 scope-completeness sweep per Gate-3 user-direction. The PRD's named four reviewers (shared-document-reviewer, review-architecture-auditor, review-cross-artifact-auditor, execute-phase-quality-reviewer) are illustrative; the intent doc's binding framing is 'any reviewer that emits a verdict+findings pair'. The sweep ran `rg -nl 'verdict.*:' .claude/agents/` (10 hits) and per-hit inspection of output contracts. Six additional reviewer-shaped agents surfaced; three deserve FR-1 scope inclusion, three are clearer exclusions.

additional_reviewer_shaped_agents_for_FR.verdict_finding_pair_quality: CLEAN — this is the cleanest verdict+findings pair in the inventory; severity tokens include 'blocker' so the verdict-vs-findings consistency check applies directly (APPROVED + any blocker finding is the contradiction FR-1 names).
additional_reviewer_shaped_agents_for_FR.blast_radius_per_invocation: Per-task; T2 dispatch; consumed by recipe-feature-pipeline.
additional_reviewer_shaped_agents_for_FR.recommendation: STRONG candidate for FR-1 scope. Excluding it would leave the execution-side per-task path open to the exact failure mode US-1 names.

additional_reviewer_shaped_agents_for_FR.findings_shape: adr_cross_location_findings[] + reviewer_findings[] (the latter is a chained pass-through from shared-document-reviewer's output)
additional_reviewer_shaped_agents_for_FR.verdict_finding_pair_quality: MEDIUM — the verdict is the packager's own but the findings are chained from a downstream reviewer (shared-document-reviewer with doc_type: DeliverableArchive). A 'PASS + chained reviewer_findings with blocker' would be the contradiction.
additional_reviewer_shaped_agents_for_FR.blast_radius_per_invocation: Once per feature run at Deliverable Packaging; consumed by the Final Approval Gate.
additional_reviewer_shaped_agents_for_FR.recommendation: MODERATE candidate for FR-1 scope. The chained-findings shape complicates the consistency check — if the chained shared-document-reviewer already passed the FR-1 check at its own invocation, re-checking at the packager may be redundant. Design-claude-code should make a deliberate inclusion/exclusion call.

additional_reviewer_shaped_agents_for_FR.findings_field_present: indirect — adjacent fields are confidence, dissent_evidence, violates_constraint
additional_reviewer_shaped_agents_for_FR.verdict_finding_pair_quality: WEAK — this is verdict-per-CLAIM (many verdicts inside a critique JSON), not verdict-per-INVOCATION. The intent doc's framing of 'a reviewer that emits a verdict+findings pair' is plausibly interpretable to exclude this shape, but a stricter reading includes it.

agents_with_verdict_keyword_but_clearer_.reason_excluded: USES verdicts (consumes critic's per-claim verdicts) but DOES NOT EMIT them in a verdict+findings pair contract. Its output is decision-framing JSON.

deprecation_finding.implications_for_FR_3_design: Per AC-FR-3-c, 'If ADR-0041 contains no prescription for a server present in .mcp.json (or vice-versa), then the system shall emit a blocking finding naming the unmatched server and the side on which the prescription is missing.' Under the natural reading, FR-3's parity rule would emit a BLOCKER finding on day one against mcp-openapi-schema as 'prescribed-in-ADR-0041 but absent-from-.mcp.json'. This is a false-positive against a deliberately-decided removal. Design-claude-code under U-3 has three options: (a) define a 'status' / 'deprecated' marker convention for ADR-0041 rows and have the parity rule recognize it (the in-rule approach; preserves ADR-0041's append-only discipline per ADR-0005 by adding an annotation, not removing a row); (b) amend ADR-0041 to drop the mcp-openapi-schema row entirely (out-of-scope per carve-out posture; an ADR amendment is not a quick-wins-hardening artifact); (c) maintain an allowlist of known-deprecated row identifiers inside the audit_op11 script (the most localized but least transparent option). The CLAUDE.md framing ('stale-doc issue, not an active server') points toward (a) — a status marker convention is the durable fix and treats the same problem the project will face for any future deprecated ADR row. design-claude-code picks under U-3.
